blocks.text: Explain how streaming updates flow from the backend into a buffered store, then into UI components on a controlled cadence.
A StreamClient ingests events into a buffer. A DashboardStore coalesces updates and exposes derived state to UI widgets like ProgressBar, MetricChart, and LogList.

Boundary checks:
- Validate event identity and sequence before updating any projection.
- One normalized TrainingRun store separates authoritative lifecycle, bounded metrics and logs, and connection state.
- Summary, chart, phase, and log widgets subscribe to derived slices instead of owning copies.
- Reconnect resumes from the acknowledged contiguous cursor; a gap triggers replay or snapshot recovery before that cursor advances.

blocks.code:
Run snapshot (through sequence N, resume cursor C)
  -> StreamAdapter
  -> event validator + replay dedupe + gap detector
  -> RunReducer
       -> lifecycle entity
       -> bounded metric-series cache
       -> bounded log cache
       -> freshness and cursor state
  -> selectors
       -> summary and progress
       -> downsampled charts
       -> virtualized logs
       -> accessible text/table alternatives

steps.text: Reduce authoritative events in order, then coalesce chart and log paints according to measured cost. Terminal, error, and gap events are never discarded.

blocks.title: Stream and projection ownership
blocks.text: A realtime dashboard is about buffering and batching. If you can explain how to avoid per-event re-renders, you are answering the core of this question.
Worked example: late metric after run failure

Run r9 reports failed at sequence 840, then a delayed loss sample with sequence 839 arrives after reconnect. The dashboard must retain the terminal fact without discarding valid historical evidence or implying training resumed.

blocks.title: Scenario walkthrough
rows: Normalize run and bounded metric series with cursor c838.
Charts and summary render as live.
Mark run terminal with field sequence 840.
Header shows failed and stops live elapsed time.
Insert historical sample if unseen but do not lower lifecycle sequence.
Chart gains one earlier point; header stays failed.
Fields merge by their own revision.
No duplicate error or announcement appears.
